newsitem.title: JAPAN: HANDBALL-RUSSIA TO PLAY FRANCE IN SEMI-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: HANDBALL-RUSSIA TO PLAY FRANCE IN SEMI-FINALS.

text.p: Undefeated Russia and present world champions France advanced on Thursday to a semifinal clash in the men's handball World Championship.
In the other semifinal to be played on Saturday, Hungary will meet Sweden.
The undefeated Russians crushed Asian powerhouse South Korea 32-15 in their quarter-final match. France also had a comfortable win over Egypt 22-19.
"Our defence was great today and a good defence leads to good counter-attack," Russian coach Vladimir Maximov said.
He singled out goalkeeper Andrei Lavrov, as well as Viacheslav Atavin and Oleg Grebnev for setting up a strong and tall wall of defense before the fast-moving Korean players.
France still lacked their best form against Egypt
"We made many mistakes in our offense and kept missing goals," said French coach Daniel Costantini.
"I guess we have a 25 percent chance of beating Russia," he added.
Stephane Stoecklin top-scored for the French team with five goals, followed by Philippe Julia with four.
In the first two quarter-finals, Sweden beat Olympic bronze medallist Spain 28-24 in extra time, while Hungary won 26-25 against Iceland.
Stefan Lovgren led the Swedes with six goals, while Steffan Olsson, Pierre Thorsson and Magnus Wislander each had five.
The score was tied 21-all at the start of extra time but the Swedes showed more stamina to net seven swift goals in the 10 minutes of extra time.
Zoltan Bergendi and Jozsef Eles scored five goals apiece as Hungary handed Iceland their first defeat in the championship and a surprise exit from the tournament.
After saturday's semifinals, the final will be played on Saturday.
